# SaltStack Fundamentals
SaltStack is an infrastructure automation platform. This skill covers the core concepts.
## Architecture - **Salt Master**: Central server that controls minions. Stores states in `/srv/salt/`. - **Salt Minion**: Agent running on each managed machine. Connects to master on ports 4505-4506. - **Salt API**: REST interface to Salt (port 8377 default). Used by Odoo tools.
## Core Concepts
### States (.sls files) YAML files defining desired system state. Use Jinja2 for templating. ```yaml install_nginx: pkg.installed: - name: nginx service.running: - name: nginx - enable: True - require: - pkg: install_nginx ```
### Pillar Key/value data assigned to minions. Secrets live here, never in states. ```yaml # pillar/odoo.sls odoo: admin_password: "secret123" version: "18" ```
### Grains System information about each minion (OS, CPU, IP, roles). Auto-detected. Common grains: id, os, osrelease, ipv4, roles, dc, customer.
### top.sls Maps states and pillars to minions. ```yaml base: 'gw*': - caddy 'lxd-odoo-*': - odoo.18 ```
### Requisites - `require`: Run this AFTER another state - `watch_in`: Restart service when config changes - `unless`: Only run if condition is false
### Jinja2 in States ```yaml {% set version = pillar.get('odoo.version', '18') %} install_odoo_{{ version }}: pkg.installed: - name: odoo-{{ version }} ```
## Best Practices 1. Secrets in pillar, NEVER in state files 2. Use `test.ping` before applying states 3. Preview with `state.show_sls` before `state.apply` 4. Use `unless` guards for idempotency 5. Group by function in subdirectories: caddy/, odoo/, postgres/

# Salt Remote Execution
Execute commands and modules across your infrastructure.
## Execution Modules
### test.ping Check if minions are reachable. ```bash salt '*' test.ping # All minions salt 'gw*' test.ping # Gateways only salt 'sparv' test.ping # Single minion ```
### cmd.run Execute shell commands remotely. ```bash salt '*' cmd.run 'uptime' salt 'sparv' cmd.run 'df -h' salt 'lxd-*' cmd.run 'free -m' ```
### service Manage systemd services. ```bash salt 'sparv' service.status odoo salt 'gw0' service.restart caddy salt '*' service.status salt-minion ```
### grains Read system information. ```bash salt '*' grains.items # All grains salt 'sparv' grains.get os # Specific grain salt 'gw*' grains.get roles # Roles on gateways ```
### pillar Read configuration data. ```bash salt 'sparv' pillar.items # All pillar data salt 'gw0' pillar.get caddy # Caddy config ```
### state Manage configuration. ```bash salt 'sparv' state.apply odoo.update salt 'gw0' state.show_sls caddy.service # Preview salt '*' state.highstate # Apply everything ```
## Targeting - `*` — all minions - `gw*` — glob (starts with gw) - `G@os:Ubuntu` — grain filter - `L@sparv,gw0` — list - `E@sparv\d+` — regex

# Salt State Management
Writing effective Salt states.
## State File Structure ``` /srv/salt/ ├── top.sls # Orchestration entry point ├── caddy/ │ ├── init.sls # Include other states │ ├── install.sls # Package installation │ ├── service.sls # Service management │ └── sites/ │ └── example.yaml # Site config ├── odoo/ │ ├── 18.sls # Odoo 18 installation │ ├── config.sls # Configuration │ └── repos/ # Repository files └── lxd/ └── init.sls # Container management ```
## State Functions Common state functions: - `pkg.installed` — install package - `pkg.purged` — remove package - `file.managed` — create/manage file - `file.directory` — create directory - `service.running` — ensure service runs - `service.dead` — ensure service stops - `cmd.run` — execute command - `cron.present` — schedule cron job
## Requisites (Dependencies) ```yaml service_running: service.running: - name: nginx - require: - pkg: install_nginx # Must install first - watch: - file: nginx_config # Restart if config changes ```
## Jinja2 Patterns ```yaml # Conditional {% if grains['os'] == 'Ubuntu' %} install_ubuntu_pkg: pkg.installed: - name: my-package {% endif %}
# Loops {% for user in pillar['users'] %} create_user_{{ user }}: user.present: - name: {{ user }} {% endfor %}
# Default values {% set port = pillar.get('app.port', 8080) %} ```
## Idempotency States must be safe to re-run: - Use `unless:` for one-time operations - Use `onlyif:` for conditional execution - Check before creating

# Salt Pillar & Secrets
Managing configuration data and secrets in SaltStack.
## Pillar Structure ``` /srv/salt/pillar/ ├── top.sls # Pillar assignment ├── servers.sls # Server config ├── odoo.sls # Odoo passwords ├── bifrost.sls # AI gateway config └── caddy/ └── sites.sls # Site-specific config ```
## Pillar Assignment (pillar/top.sls) ```yaml base: 'gw*': - caddy - caddy.sites 'odoo-*': - odoo '*': - servers ```
## Accessing Pillar in States ```yaml {% set admin_password = pillar['odoo']['admin_password'] %} {% set version = pillar.get('odoo.version', '18') %}
configure_odoo: file.managed: - name: /etc/odoo/odoo.conf - template: jinja - defaults: admin_password: {{ admin_password }} version: {{ version }} ```
## Secret Management
### NEVER commit secrets to Git Secrets belong in protected pillar or external pillar: ```yaml # /srv/salt/pillar/protected/secrets.sls (NOT in git) bifrost: secrets: providers: openrouter: "sk-or-..." openai: "sk-..." ```
### Secret Reference Pattern Use symbolic references in public pillar: ```yaml bifrost: providers: openrouter: secret_ref: bifrost:secrets:providers:openrouter env: BIFROST_OPENROUTER_API_KEY ```
### Keykeep Integration Pillar secrets can sync to keykeep.credential for auditing and rotation: - `salt.pillar` with data_type='secret' - Sync creates `keykeep.credential` with encryption - Version history tracks rotations

# Salt Minion Lifecycle
Managing Salt minions from creation to decommission.
## Onboarding
### Install Salt Minion ```bash # On new machine: curl -fsSL https://repo.saltproject.io/salt/py3/ubuntu/24.04/amd64/SALT-PROJECT-GPG-PUBKEY-2023.gpg | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/salt-archive-keyring.gpg echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/salt-archive-keyring.gpg] https://repo.saltproject.io/salt/py3/ubuntu/24.04/amd64 latest main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/salt.list sudo apt update && sudo apt install salt-minion ```
### Configure Minion ```bash # Edit /etc/salt/minion master: saltmaster.example.com id: my-minion-name ```
### Accept Key ```bash # On master: salt-key -L # List pending keys salt-key -a my-minion -y # Accept key salt 'my-minion' test.ping # Verify ```
## Grain Management ```bash # Auto-detected (from system) salt '*' grains.items
# Custom grains in /etc/salt/grains roles: - odoo - postgres dc: ska ```
## Troubleshooting
### Minion won't connect ```bash salt 'my-minion' test.ping salt 'my-minion' cmd.run 'systemctl status salt-minion' salt 'my-minion' cmd.run 'journalctl -u salt-minion -n 50' ```
### Key mismatch ```bash # On master: salt-key -d my-minion -y # Remove old key # On minion: rm -f /etc/salt/pki/minion/minion.pem /etc/salt/pki/minion/minion.pub systemctl restart salt-minion # Back on master: salt-key -a my-minion -y ```
### Restart patterns ```bash salt '*' service.restart salt-minion # All salt 'lxd-*' service.restart salt-minion # Containers salt-call service.restart salt-minion # Local ```
## Decommissioning ```bash salt-key -d my-minion -y # Remove from master # On minion: systemctl stop salt-minion apt purge salt-minion ```

# Zabbix Monitoring Concepts
Zabbix is an enterprise monitoring platform. This skill covers the core concepts for AI-driven infrastructure operations.
## Architecture - **Zabbix Server**: Central poller and alert engine - **Zabbix Agent2**: Lightweight agent on each host (port 10050) - **Zabbix Frontend**: Web UI at https://zabbix.example.com - **Zabbix API**: JSON-RPC at /api_jsonrpc.php
## Core Concepts
### Hosts Machines being monitored. Each host has: - Hostname, IP, DNS - Host groups (e.g., "Linux servers", "Gateways") - Templates (inherited monitoring config)
### Items Individual metrics being collected: - `system.cpu.load` — CPU load - `vm.memory.size[available]` — Available memory - `net.tcp.listen[22]` — SSH port - `odoo.http.status[...]` — Odoo HTTP status - `salt.minion.running` — Salt-minion process
### Triggers Conditions that create problems: - "CPU load > 5 for 5 minutes" → Warning - "Odoo HTTP endpoint not responding" → Disaster - "No free disk space" → High
### Problems Active issues. Severity levels: - 0: Not classified - 1: Information - 2: Warning - 3: Average - 4: High - 5: Disaster
### Events Everything that happens: - Problem created/resolved - Auto-discovery events - Agent auto-registration
### Actions Automated responses: - Send email/SMS - Execute remote command - POST webhook (→ Odoo Infrastructure Operator)
## Common API Operations
### Get active problems ```python api.call("problem.get", { "output": "extend", "severities": [4, 5], "recent": True, }) ```
### Acknowledge event ```python api.call("event.acknowledge", { "eventids": ["12345"], "action": 1, "message": "Restarted odoo service" }) ```
### Get host info ```python api.call("host.get", { "output": "extend", "filter": {"host": ["sparv"]}, "selectItems": "extend", }) ```
### Get history ```python api.call("history.get", { "output": "extend", "itemids": ["54321"], "sortfield": "clock", "sortorder": "DESC", "limit": 100, }) ```
Structured 5-step Zabbix triage: problem → trigger → item history → correlation → Salt mapping. Teaches the AI how to reason from Zabbix alerts to concrete Salt diagnostic commands.

# Zabbix Troubleshooting Methodology
A structured approach to go from a Zabbix alert to concrete Salt diagnostic commands.
## The 5-Step Method
### Step 1: Start from the active problem Use zabbix_get_problems or zabbix_get_alerts to see what's currently active on the host. - What's the problem name? - What's the severity? - When did it start?
### Step 2: Look up the trigger Use zabbix_get_triggers to understand what's being measured and the threshold. - What item is monitored? - What condition triggers the alert? - Example: "Odoo HTTP endpoint not responding" → trigger checks HTTP status code
### Step 3: Check item history Use zabbix_get_history to see the metric around the problem time. - What was the normal value before the problem? - Did it spike gradually or suddenly? - Are there patterns (nightly spikes, weekends)?
### Step 4: Correlate with other problems Check for multiple problems on the same host — they may share a root cause. - Disk full + Odoo down → disk full caused Odoo to crash - CPU spike + memory high → possible memory leak - Multiple services down → possible host reboot or power issue
### Step 5: Map to Salt diagnostic commands Translate Zabbix triggers into concrete Salt commands:
| Zabbix Trigger | Salt Diagnostic | |---|---| | Odoo HTTP not responding | salt_service_status + salt_journal_errors + tail odoo log | | No free disk space | salt_disk_usage + find large files | | CPU load too high | salt_process_list + salt_system_load | | PostgreSQL not responding | salt_cmd_run pg_isready + check replication | | Caddy 502 errors | salt_service_status caddy + curl upstream | | Memory usage > 90% | salt_memory_usage + salt_process_list (find culprit) | | SSH brute force detected | salt_journal_errors sshd + check auth.log |
## Example Triage Flow
``` 1. zabbix_get_problems(host='sparv') → "Odoo HTTP endpoint not responding" (severity 5) 2. zabbix_get_triggers → trigger checks net.tcp.service[http,8069] 3. zabbix_get_history(itemid, time_from=1h ago) → HTTP status was 200, dropped to 0 at 14:32 4. zabbix_get_problems(host='sparv') → also "No free disk space" (severity 4) — CORRELATION! 5. Salt: salt_disk_usage('sparv') → /var/log 95% full → find large files → odoo.log 20GB Root cause: disk full → Odoo couldn't write logs → crashed Fix: rotate logs → restart odoo → verify ```
